title: Paralysis/knockout message suppression resets a different variable

impact.description: C reactions can remain suppressed after recovery; no actual later death/decision change observed.

notes: Older imported C resets the global correctly. This is a newer C regression, not a Neo omission.

references.description: reported C observation; not an independent validation

reference.description: reported C observation; not an independent validation

reported_sources.text:
`borg-messages.c` sets the global `borg_dont_react` on "You have been
  knocked out." and "You are paralyzed"; `borg_react()`
  (`borg-messages-react.c`) then queues nothing and only notes "# Ignoring
  messages.". The reset in `borg.c` (`borg_inkey_hack` path:
  `borg.dont_react = false;`) clears the unused struct field
  `borg.dont_react` instead, so once set the global stays true for the rest
  of the process: the Borg never again queues hit/miss/kill/SELF messages
  for `borg_update()`, and `borg_caution()` notes "# Borg ignoring messges."
  every turn. By code reading; the full suite never sets it (checked with
  a temporary log of the flag).

next_at_import: Retain a legal/reachable normal-rule scenario, initialization/pins, actual before/after commands/outcomes and negative controls before marking a fix validated.
